When to Contact a Denver Burn Injury Lawyer

Not all burn injuries will make you eligible for financial compensation in Colorado. If you believe that someone else was negligent (careless) and that this caused your burn injury, however, consult with an attorney about a possible personal injury lawsuit. It is especially important to hire a lawyer if you suffered severe burns that will most likely cause scarring, disfigurement, or debilitation. A
Denver injury attorney
will have the resources and abilities to thoroughly investigate your burn injury, determine fault and negotiate for fair compensation on your behalf.
Types of Burn Injuries

There are four types of burn injuries based on the cause of the injury, as well as three classifications based on burn severity. Burns can be thermal, chemical, electrical, or from sources of radiation:
Thermal burns – the number one type – are from sources of heat energy, such as hot objects or steam.
Chemical burns are from acidic or basic chemicals that are caustic enough to harm the skin.
Electrical burns stem from sources of electrical energy, such as a power line.
Radiation burns can occur from contact with x-rays or UV rays.

The three types of burn severity are first, second, and third-degree burns. First-degree burns are the least severe. They typically do not cause permanent scarring or damage. Second-degree burns are more serious and require professional medical care. They cause blistering and may scar. Third-degree burns are the most severe. Third-degree burns can damage the deeper tissues and muscles, causing permanent disfigurement, debilitation or death.
Common Causes of Burn Injuries in Denver

Most serious burn injuries in Denver are preventable. They stem from careless, reckless or malicious acts. If an employer fails to properly train or prepare employees to handle dangerous materials at work, for example, the employer could be responsible for related burn injuries. Some of the most common causes in Denver include:
Fires and explosions
Automobile
and
truck accidents
Contact with hot objects or steam
Defective products
Dangerous premises
Workplace incidents
Chemical spills
Electrical malfunctions

If one or more parties had the power to prevent your burn injuries, that party may be liable – legally and financially responsible – for your related losses. Liability for a burn injury in Denver could go to a product manufacturer, property owner, employer, driver, the government or a combination of parties, depending on the case. You may need an attorney’s assistance to determine liability for your burn injury.
Types of Compensation Available for Burn Victims

If you or your attorney succeeds in holding someone responsible for your burn injury in Denver, you could recover financial compensation for many past and future losses. Your attorney can help you create a full list of your compensable losses or damages to submit with your insurance claim. Examples of the damages that may be available in a burn injury claim in Colorado include:
Medical expenses: health care costs, such as an ambulance ride, trip to the emergency room, overnight hospital stay, surgeries, skin grafts, medications, physical therapy and rehabilitation.
Disability: the long-term or permanent effects of a burn injury, such as disfiguring scars, contractures, loss of mobility, nervous system disorders or an amputation.
Lost wages: losses of income and diminished future capacity to earn due to a significant burn injury that makes it impossible to return to your job.

Property damage: if the incident that gave you a burn injury also damaged your property, such as a house fire or car crash, you may qualify for compensation to pay for property repairs or replacement.

Pain and suffering: the noneconomic damages associated with your burns, which may be significant. These can include physical pain, chronic pain, emotional distress, mental anguish, diminished quality of life, loss of consortium and reduced enjoyment of life.

If the defendant is guilty of gross negligence, malicious intent to harm or a wanton disregard for your safety, you may also receive punitive damages from a judge. This is an additional award granted to punish a defendant. Discuss the potential value of your burn injury claim with an attorney before entering into settlement negotiations with an insurance company to better protect yourself financially.
How a Denver Burn Injury Lawyer Can Help

Consulting with an attorney at the beginning of your burn injury claim can make it easier to recover the financial compensation that you deserve. If your injury requires future foreseeable medical costs or has significantly impacted your life, it is even more important to work with an attorney during the legal process. An attorney can prevent an insurance company from taking advantage of you. Your lawyer can use aggressive negotiation tactics to fight for the compensation that you deserve.

In addition to seeking maximum financial compensation on your behalf, your lawyer can connect you to top burn injury doctors and specialists in Denver. Meanwhile, the law firm will work to investigate your accident and collect evidence of negligence to support your injury claim. Your attorney will handle the complicated legal legwork of your case while you focus on recuperating from a serious burn. You will benefit from greater peace of mind during this difficult time with a lawyer in your corner.
How Long You Have to File a Burn Injury Claim

It is important to realize that you do not have an unlimited amount of time in which to file a burn injury claim in Denver, Colorado. The state’s statute of limitations gives you a maximum of two years from the date of the accident or injury to file a related claim. If you do not bring your civil lawsuit within two years, you will most likely forfeit the right to seek a financial recovery.

There are some exceptions, however, in special cases, such as a burned minor (two years from the date of his or her 18th birthday) or a case against the government (180 days). Some exceptions extend the deadline while others shorten it. This is why it is wise to contact a personal injury lawyer in Denver as soon as possible about a potential burn injury claim – before it’s too late.
